name: Richard Lyons
description: A wealthy London vintner and royal financial adviser, previously convicted of corruption in the Good Parliament of 1376 and pardoned. Killed by the rebels in London on or around 14 June 1381 -- named in chronicle accounts among the officials specifically hunted down, in contrast to the comparatively indiscriminate killing of Flemish immigrants happening in the same days.
narrative_function: One of the named, targeted killings that distinguish the revolt's violence from an undirected mob.
